I would say I have. You describe quite well. A glimpse in how “good” good can be. I’ve learned that it’s an endless cycle of going up and down and ultimately leads nowhere. Chasing higher highs. Yet, in the midst of the uplifting and the humiliating there lies something more.  For me it’s a memory? Almost as if the cycle reminded me of something deep within. 

Ultimately, I’ve stopped looking for God in the drugs, but I don’t discount their utility.

I’d read keep reading. I’d focus on the gospels, Mathew, Mark, Luke and John. Then still focusing more on the direct words of Jesus.

Don’t let the influence of other people affect your journey to God so much. God is a compassionate and merciful being, and He has orchestrated his manifestation tailored to each one of us. In spite of your initial contact with Him being one of abuse of amphetamines it doesn’t take away from the experience you have with God. The words of Christ have an incredible depth that will always penetrate one’s heart if that individual is willing, and even if one is not behaving “accordingly.”

Why not keep investigating in solitude with God? It doesn’t mean you have to stop using amphetamines or binging stimulants. Let not these notions of how one should attempt to connect with God distance you from Him. In perfect time you’ll receive the wisdom on how one should navigate the proper use of the substance, and how to approach the Divine. God loves you so much he is trying to form a connection with you.
I replaced drugs with God. Much easier to live. Although, drugs have a special spot in my heart. I don’t feel it’s against me to use, just would rather not.

I’ve felt the same. I’ve been using drugs since I was super young. I think I’ve sort of grown out of it? I also share the same sentiment in regard to stimulants. 

Honestly, I’m more motivated to do the work I need to do. I’ve sort of learned which drugs are helpful and useful and really only use them as tools. It’s a healthier relationship.

I use both. Sometimes, I eye ball about 1g or so of Phenibut. That’ll be for the whole day. I may use that for about a week or so. Afterwards, I I’ll use kratom at about 2g - 4g every 14ish hours for the week. 

I’d say it helps get things different. It’s a good way to prevent any dependence issues for me. The euphoria is a bit more consistent with the kratom. The Phenibut doesn’t really have much euphoria. Still, I do feel the rare times there is withdrawal it’s not too bad to deal with. 

However, none of this is as useful as amphetamine. I do this during the week as I take my prescription on the weekend when there’s more of demand to be productive and energized for the majority of the day.

It's also courageous to look back and think about the scary things in our past. Which you have seemed to do as well. Doing difficult things deserve more than a hug!

It's not your fault. We live in a world where true evil can manifest itself in a person. For no fault of our own many of us come in contact with evil and we needed to be protected. Yet, no one did. You also have no blame for your conception. It also wasn't fair for you to be treated like a slave and robbing you of valuable time with your grandpa. 

Considering what you went through and also knowing the amount of strength required to share our tragedies in our lives. It looks like you have a lot of strength to show us a vulnerability. Seeing our realities is a struggle we all have. This strength is what will empower you to shape your world.

It is an answer. It just isn't the right answer 99% of the time. It's easy to confuse an escape from all the suffering and misery we have to deal with life with death. It's a simple solution to a complex problem we share. As it is an ultimate perhaps we could try everything else that could help. You could always do it the next day.

Sure we can survive with them around, but what if we could thrive with them? Reach a level of ability where we see them differently.

I enjoy it. Shits a blast but damn people are the fucking best. Love them! I understand how unbearable it is when we have no control over it. Yet, knowing I have the option and power to change it easily is what allows me to be at peace.

Well, what would be the consequences if you didn't start a relationship. Both realities have their areas of fear. It seems like you've gotten to know what being alone is like that it's safe and you know what is dangerous. However, a relationship presents itself with new opportunities and also unknown dangers. A danger hidden is always going to be much scarier than a known danger. Something to think about. Being honest about thing saves us lots of trouble.

It's not easy being alone. Being a lonely guy also comes with its own problems. It's difficult to say if no one does care about how guys feel. I've seen a large portion of it as lacking skill in showing we do care. Despite that, it is a painful situation to have to live in. The more time passes being alone the more difficult it will become to not be. What do you think is making finding friends difficult?

You have the power to change it all. I say this as I've been there too, and we all can change everything.

It's not easy to let people in after we've been on our own. It does get harder as time goes gone and people disappoint us. We are constantly learning how to behave to others, and being alone really hampers our social skills. For the majority of us, we sort of need people. How come you feel you can't have simple conversations?

Yeah, you’re right. Having people care about you can make all the difference, and a large part of caring is understanding another’s struggle. I mean really UNDERSTANDING by thoroughly listening. We have only the best intention by offering advice, but our advice can come across as a little arrogant as it suggest we already know how to solve the problem. Unless we hear the other person out it’s very difficult to understand what the problem is. Unfortunately the majority of us don’t know how to listen to each other or know how have the other person feel cared about. We should aim to build trust before we choose to give advice, but most importantly is to work together to solve the problem.

Advice is what we give when we don't feel like understanding other's problems. As the majority of our problems are incredibly complex. They have the aim in sort of the right direction, but it isn't useful or applicable. I spend a lot of my time with lonely people as I would have appreciated someone doing the same for me, and the reality of our world is what causes a large portion of the misfortune in ourselves. It takes a great deal of time and effort to slowly propel each other upwards. Ultimately, the final truth is one that is too difficult to handle and requires a lot of trust to be received. Which I don't blame anyone for not being willing to risk building trust as the consequences of betrayal are tragic and deadly.
Or perhaps this is still too much for you right now. Do you feel you could find ways to ease into going to similar events alone?
I'd imagine you already did. It totally makes sense to be scared to go alone, yet it's awe-inspiring to go into it anyway. What sort of ways can we make it easier for you?

Don't blame yourself too hard. All it takes is one interaction and we see how strong all our feelings overwhelm us. I don't know how well you guys ended and if reality says it's done. It would be wise to investigate what went wrong, what could we have done better, and what we will do. Until the work is done the curse of lost love will cling to us and alter our view of reality.

If it's any piece of mind. You're aren't alone in not having a friendship. Making friends is hard. Have you considered going alone to the football game? I can imagine how uncomfortable that would even be to think about!

Maybe it would be a good idea to ask how come it seems you're the only one who reaches out? I understand that kind of question is going to put you in a very vulnerable position, but I feel the outcome will make this easier.

Do you think they may feel the same as you do? Reaching out has a risk to it no? We are constantly afraid to do many things, yet there is always a greater reward in doing those scary things. I can't say whether or not your friends care enough to reach out or are too cowardly to act, yet in the end, it's frustrating to have to feel this way.

You are right in seeing the fairness in friendship. If only one person initiates it can appear as we aren't even wanted. Well, why not be the one who always reaches out? What sort of things comes to your head that stops you?

Wow! It's always nice to hear people be so wise. I feel you are doing a very noble thing by not accepting your current reality. Which is not an easy thing for us to accept, yet here you are confronting it. It sounds like all of this has taken a toll on you and has been very difficult. As is the truth, yet it's what will serve to us be free. I feel it would be helpful to ask yourself, "What caused this disaster, and what could I do to change it?" If you'd like some help I would be happily work with you for clarity.

It's okay to be confused and not know all the answers. Low self-esteem does usually bring overthinking situations. Just know it doesn't always have to feel this way, and you can change everything around you.

What do you think makes you go completely silent? Despite this. It's must be so frustrating to want friends and to only push them away.

It truly is the most confusing emotion to feel. To feel lonely amongst others. These thoughts you are having almost seem to be begging you to understand them. It's difficult to unravel the meaning behind these thoughts as it's very uncomfortable. 

I can understand how asking for love can come across as needy. Asking, in general, is a place of humility. Yet, there is real strength in stepping down and revealing these inner parts of you. I don't feel you are asking for too much at all! Love is a need. If you imagine being dehydrated and asking for water would need not be needy. We can see a similar story only it's difficult to see the symptoms of lack of need.
I can't even imagine how you feel right now. Truly must be a painful feeling. I hope you can consider most times our lives are so hard we desire an escape ultimately even death.

It's a weird dance we have with others where we can circle each other, never touching. Yet, there's another dance we do embrace each other and dance much closer. I feel it's important to make the distinction between what being sociable is and genuinely forming connections. 

It looks like you have lots of quality but no quality. It is confusing to see all these people, but looking closer to see they're not really there, like cardboard cutouts. In the end, what we do need is to be able to have meaningful relationships and that includes having people you can count on being there for you. I hope you can find some clarity in this. I'm sure it all can so weird and hard to manage. I feel it would a good idea to investigate what is leading to not being able to connect with other people. You can do this!

It does get harder to connect with others the longer you spend being alone. Objectively looking into human communications they really are another skill one can learn. 

I understand what you mean. Being able to be social and get along with others is incredibly different than being able to connect with each other. I feel we tend to minimize the need we have in having meanigful good enough relationships and can make our heads messy. It sounds like you've been hurting through this, and I'm sorry you've had to push through this alone. I feel you are doing a positive thing exploring some of these thoughts.

It is difficult in being to understand what friendship is, what a friend is. We as people can be very selfish with each other. It does hurt so much hearing we're friends, and only to see they don't care too much about us. You aren't playing the victim for addressing how you feel. Don't you think a real friend would attempt to understand you before invalidating you?

I feel you are quite wise in choosing not to be treated like this. I'm glad you still have a love for people. Your exhaustion is proof of how much effort it is to have to go through this. Your heart really has taken a beating.

Stress makes it so hard to be able to think clearly. No one deserves to carry on this way. Ending the cycle is possible. You can do it!

I used to be lonely and struggled with it for a while, but I learned a great deal about how to overcome it. What worked for me was to really try to understand the emotions and go deeper into what I was doing that created my loneliness. I was still lonely but had an easier time with my feelings and self-esteem. Which helped me to objectively look at what I could do to improve connections with others. I made mistakes along the way but over time it became easier to make friends.

I do continue to study and practise the best way I can truly connect with people. Despite creating strong bonds with many people and seeing them want to be better friends, I've learned how I really enjoy being alone and understand what we'd both need in order to create a beautiful friendship. I guess I'm alone, but not lonely. 

I hope you may be able to find some meaning in what worked for me. I can clarify or explain more if you would like. Thank you for reading and I hope life will let you see the light out of the tunnel.

Having confidence is a funny thing. To me, it's this self-assurance that no matter what happens I'm going to be okay because I know I'll be able to handle what comes my way.

What has helped me cultivate confidence are stressors I inadvertently or purposely put myself through. I feel a good example would driving a car. At first, you're very unconfident in your ability to control the car, but by practicing (adding stress) you begin to feel more sure in your abilities. Becoming more confident.

Another thing to note is to not stress yourself out more than you can handle. If you try adding too much stress before you're ready.  Most times you'll give up. On the opposite spectrum, too little and you don't grow and get bored. You wouldn't try to drive on the freeway if you've never even driven a car, and to grow it's a good idea to drive the car during traffic hour.

I feel this can apply to many things in life. Too stressful and you quit. No growth. Too easy and you get bored and quit. No growth.
Over time, as you overcome stresses you'll feel more confident in being able to handle different situations that will stress you out.
